title: Learning scales with a trumpet-playing friend
summary: In Charleston he studied scales on a blackboard at the home of trumpeter Samuel Walker, whose father taught at Jenkins'.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Mm hmm. And, we got married. And, then I used to -- while I was --- a friend of mine was a trumpet player, and as far as studying music was concerned, I used to go over to his house. And, we would have a blackboard.
In Charleston. And, we would go through the routine of the scales, and what not -- music.
Yes. And, we would do this.
Yeah. And started you reading music a bit?

Yes. Yes. And, then there was a group called the Nighthawks in Charleston, and the trumpet player's father was one of the teachers at Jenkins'. His son -- his name was Samuel Walker And, he was a terrific trumpet player, so he had this group -- let's see -- trumpet, -- drums, -- saxophone, I think, -- piano. Four pieces I think it was. And, they were getting ready to do some dances at a place called Darts Hall.
I don't know whether there was -- it has anything to do with where I lived, -- all that -- you know.
But, that was the name of the hall -- Darts Hall.
